Want to turn a dull, gray photo into something that really stands out? Here’s a quick guide:
	1.	Pick a photo you like, even if it feels a little flat.
	2.	Adjust the basics—brightness, contrast, shadows, and saturation—just enough to make it come alive.
	3.	Play with color. Add a warm or cool tone, or make one part of the photo pop with a color splash.
	4.	Get creative with textures, overlays, or selective edits to give it an artistic feel.
	5.	Finish strong: crop, straighten, and sharpen so it looks polished.
	6.	Share it! Try a caption like: “From gray to glow. Who knew a little edit could change everything?”

No fancy tools required—just your phone and a bit of creativity. Give it a try and tag me; I’d love to see your transformations.

It begins like any other stop: an old yellow-brick building transformed into Mercato—shops and dining.

The sign invites you inside.
The iron gate is already open.

Nothing about it feels dangerous yet.

Then you step back and see how enormous it really is.

Before the restaurants, boutiques and apartments, these walls belonged to a sprawling hospital complex. Thousands of lives once passed behind the identical windows and beneath the red towers.

The building has been restored.

But restoration is not the same as forgetting

Inside, daylight disappears.

The hallways glow beneath mismatched lamps. Old brick, exposed pipes and numbered mailboxes remain while footsteps echo from somewhere just beyond the next corner.

The lights are warm.

The feeling is not.

The shops try to make the old corridors feel ordinary.

A stuffed alpaca watches from the wall. A strange black creature stares from a shelf. A bright red alarm waits beneath the words:

PULL IN CASE OF FIRE.

For a moment, everything feels playful—until you realize every object seems to be looking back.

Farther inside, the building grows quieter.

A single plant sits beneath an amber light, placed carefully against bricks that have outlived everyone who first walked these halls.

It looks decorative.

It also looks like someone wanted to hide whatever was behind it.

At the end, the transformation is complete.

The marketplace is gone.
The voices are gone.
Only the empty corridor remains.

You entered a restored piece of history, but somewhere between the shops and the silence, it began to feel like the building was restoring something too—

a memory of itself.

And as you turn to leave, one final thought follows you:

Maybe the halls were never empty. Maybe they were only waiting for someone to notice.

One of the hardest product shoots I’ve pulled off, but I’m really happy with how these turned out.

Shot for @twistedpendant , featuring their Italian 925 Silver Cuban Chain (5MM) and Italian 925 Silver Cuban Bracelet (5MM).

I really wanted to do this shoot right because jewelry is a market I’ve been wanting to break into, and I wanted to make a strong first impression. That meant spending sooo much extra time on the concept, lighting, motion, reflections, and the small details that make silver jewelry actually look good on camera. I have learned ALOT through this experience.
